source_review.notes: Checked all seven references against official protobuf.dev documentation. The encoding guide supports tag/wire-type arithmetic, field-order nondeterminism, and framing/resource facts; the proto3/editions guides support numbering, reservation, presence, unknown retention, and safe/conditional/unsafe change classes; best practices supports permanent tag identity and conservative enums/types; ProtoJSON and techniques support distinct JSON/framing rules. The official support matrix records Edition 2026 released 20 August 2026 with minimum protoc 36.0 and distinguishes editions from runtime release lines.

evidence: Checked S_v, W_v, R_v, m, b, N, Q, U_v, M_v, tag t, number n, and wire type w for consistent domains.
Confirmed shift, bitwise-or/and, universal-pair, intersection, encoding/decoding, and semantic-preservation expressions use defined notation.
Confirmed wire-safe, wire-compatible, wire-unsafe, presence, unknown field, semantic compatibility, version skew, and reservation terms are defined.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently separates bytes, schema interpretation, path preservation, and domain meaning.

evidence: Recomputed tag 8 as field 1 and wire type 0: 8 >> 3 = 1 and 8 & 7 = 0.
Recomputed varint bytes 0x96 0x01 as (0x16) + (1 << 7) = 22 + 128 = 150.
Checked tag 42 in Exercise 1 as field 5/type 2 and verified the documented 1–15 compact range and 19000–19999 reserved range against official guidance.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic is exact wire-format reasoning; no empirical size, speed, or compatibility rate is claimed.

evidence: Expanded tag=(n<<3)|w and recovered n=tag>>3 and w=tag&7 for valid three-bit wire types.
Checked N intersection Q is empty as the field-allocation/reservation invariant.
Checked the supported writer/reader/path predicate requires parsing, bounds, preservation, and semantic invariants rather than parse success alone.
Verified number-reuse ambiguity follows because binary records contain number/wire type/payload but no former schema name or meaning.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Derivations are scoped to protobuf's documented binary model and declared supported paths.

evidence: Reviewed absent versus explicitly default scalars, minimum/maximum and negative integers, unknown enums/fields, packed/unpacked repeated data, maps, oneofs, empty/nested/oversized messages, malformed/truncated/overlong varints, and UTF-8.
Reviewed old/new direct readers, old relays, field-by-field copies, binary/JSON/TextFormat transformations, queues, archives, snapshots, rollback, offline clients, and ten-year devices.

Reviewed field-number/type/unit reuse, conflicting dual fields, authorization-sensitive additions, unknown-data trust boundaries, decompression/resource abuse, toolchain skew, and deterministic-byte misuse.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans representation, semantics, deployment, persistence, language/runtime, gateway, and adversarial-resource boundaries.

evidence: Executed protobuf-tag-varint and confirmed the exact field, wire type, and value outputs.
Confirmed all removal guidance permanently reserves numbers and relevant names; no example permits tag reuse.
Confirmed additive changes retain tolerant old behavior, unknown preservation is path-specific, and semantic changes require a fresh field/message or migration.
Confirmed deployment orders tolerant readers before writers, preserves rollback, tests stored replay, and gates required semantics until old writers leave support.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable verifies encoding arithmetic; production compatibility still requires descriptors, generated runtimes, fixtures, paths, and domain evidence.

evidence: Reviewed unknown-field skipping: wire type supplies payload extent, conditional on well-formed bounded input and a preserving runtime/path.
Reviewed number-reuse impossibility: without external schema/version evidence, identical field number/wire records cannot reveal whether old or new meaning was intended.
Reviewed the compatibility predicate and confirmed descriptor checks prove only structural subsets, not business-semantic preservation.
proof_review.notes: The chapter gives valid bounded arguments and explicitly states implementation/path assumptions.

evidence: Confirmed binary-safe, conditionally compatible, source/JSON, and semantic claims are kept distinct.
Confirmed shared wire type is never presented as proof of declared-type compatibility.
Confirmed the decoder is labeled as arithmetic evidence, while rolling, cross-language, performance, security, and storage claims require separate tests.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Guarantees and limitations are labeled at each change class and mechanism boundary.

evidence: Snippet report artifacts/snippets/API-052/report.json records one passing deterministic Python wire-decoding run.
Edition 2026 release date/minimum compiler and current support lines are attributed to the retrieved official support matrix.
Live producer/consumer fleets, archived bytes, gateways, generated runtimes, performance, fuzzing, rollback, and clinical workflows remain future case-specific evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production schema registry, toolchain, device, service, database, queue, gateway, or archive was empirically tested.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed wire records, two-direction compatibility, presence, enums, unknown preservation, composite fields, schema ownership, rollout, editions/toolchains, resource validation, and evidence matrices as a coherent evolution method that distinguishes structural from semantic compatibility.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked practitioner utility through permanent reservations, additive replacement, deterministic dual-read precedence, reader-before-writer rollout, rollback/retention gates, descriptor lint, golden cross-version/language/relay tests, pinned compiler/plugins/runtimes, stored replay, bounded parsing, canary telemetry, and explicit unknown-data trust policy.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module derives tag mechanics before compatibility, then develops presence/enums/unknowns/composite structures, ownership, deployment, tooling, security, and verification. Ten examples cover distinct arithmetic, additive, reuse, semantic-unit, relay, enum, oneof, canonicalization, old-client, and edition cases; five exercises culminate in ten-year medical-device transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
